title: VerificationResult::is_verified() returns true if ANY signer passed — security-critical callers cannot use it safely
description:
## Problem

In `smime-tree/src/error.rs`, `VerificationResult::is_verified()` returns:

```rust
pub fn is_verified(&self) -> bool {
    self.signers.iter().any(|s| matches!(s.status, SignerStatus::Verified))
}
```

In a multi-signer `SignedData` message, this returns `true` if even one signer out of N passed verification. A message where all expected signers failed verification (or are completely unknown to the caller) but a single injected unknown signer happened to verify would return `is_verified() == true`.

## Concrete attack scenario

An attacker who can inject a `SignerInfo` for a certificate they control into a `SignedData` blob:
1. Caller's expected signer: Bob (fails — signature invalid or unknown cert)
2. Attacker's injected signer: attacker's cert (passes — valid signature from attacker)
3. `is_verified()` returns `true`

The attacker has made an unauthenticated message appear verified.

## What the API name implies

The method name `is_verified` implies 'this message has been verified'. What it actually checks is 'at least one of possibly many unknown signers passed their own verification'. These are completely different security properties.

## Missing contract documentation

The doc comment on `is_verified` does not state this ANY-signer semantic. Callers who read the name and use it as a boolean gate — the overwhelmingly common pattern — will have a security vulnerability.

## What goes wrong if left as-is

Security-critical callers will write `if result.is_verified() { ... }` and believe the message was authenticated by the expected signer(s). Callers must instead inspect `result.signers` individually and verify that their specific expected signer's certificate appears with `SignerStatus::Verified`, but nothing in the API surface makes this obvious or required.

## Files

- `smime-tree/src/error.rs` — `VerificationResult::is_verified()`
